# F5 · Chip season plan

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*

Identifiers in this file: `F5-AC-01` – `F5-UP-01`.

#### F5 · Chip season plan

| Section | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | **Should.** The season-plan display matters every week; the full squad-rebuild flow (F9) does not, since chips are played only a handful of times a season. |
| Serves | The first core job's chip decision in Section 2.3 — at season scale, reviewed weekly and decided rarely. |
| Happy path | The Chips tab shows a next-action widget, a plan card with one row per chip, and a short editorial under each live chip. A *generate proposal* control on the Wildcard and Free Hit rows opens the chip-proposal flow (see F9). |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **F5-AC-01** | The Chips tab is advice only: no swipe gestures, no accept, nothing to confirm. |
| **F5-AC-02** | Nothing on the Chips tab enters the weekly shortlist or the NBal. |
| **F5-AC-03** | The plan changes when the fixtures change; the manager cannot override it in this version. |
| **F5-AC-04** | **The category-tab bar below the Squad/Assistant segmented control carries this screen's own tab, labelled "Chips,"** alongside Overview, Transfer, Sub and Captain. |
| **F5-AC-05** | The Chips tab's meta line shows the gameweek the decision is at (for example "GW7") while pending, or "Done" once resolved — the same pending/done convention F3 and F4 use. |
| **F5-AC-06** | **The refresh control lives in the Assistant status bar (3.1), not on the Chips tab body** — alongside the last-run time and, on this tab, a label scoped to it ("Chips") rather than the Overview's "All", matching F6's per-screen scoping rule. |
| **F5-AC-07** | **Tapping refresh opens the same confirm-before-rerun sheet F6 requires, scoped to this tab.** Title: "Refresh the Chip plan?" Scope line: "Chip plan only · 4 chips in scope." It states plainly that the week's transfer, substitution and captain calls are left untouched — only the season chip plan is rewritten. |
| **F5-AC-08** | The plan gives one row per chip in priority order, with a verdict (play, target, hold, spent) and a six-gameweek timeline of equal-width cells, tied to that chip's own verdict rather than computed independently per gameweek. |
| **F5-AC-09** | **The timeline has three cell states, not two.** The recommended week is a solid dark green; a lead-in week where the chip is a genuine possibility is a lighter translucent green; every other week is grey. A *hold* or *spent* verdict shows no green at all. |
| **F5-AC-10** | The timeline never uses amber or red. |
| **F5-AC-11** | **The distinction between the two greens must not be colour alone.** The design carries it by shade with no label or other cue, which conflicts with the Accessibility NFR. A non-colour cue distinguishing the recommended week from a merely-possible one is required before this ships. |
| **F5-AC-12** | Amber and red on this tab mean deadline pressure only — never conviction. |
| **F5-AC-13** | An expiry line states how many chips expire and when. The boundary is after Gameweek 19; once it passes all four chips refresh into a fresh set, and the timeline must show a chip becoming available again if the visible window crosses that boundary. |
| **F5-AC-14** | Spent chips carry no editorial and are shown at reduced opacity; a spent chip cannot be played again from that chip set. |
| **Unhappy Paths** |  |
| **F5-UP-01** | **A chip plan drifts from the week's accepted calls** — for example the plan assumes a Bench Boost while an accepted transfer sells a bench player. Acceptance: a known, monitored risk for this version rather than designed around — chips are never accepted or played in the app (see F9), so there is no played chip for a transfer to undermine. |
